subject: Svenska
title: Reading comprehension
sourceSummary: Finding information in a text, understanding what it is broadly about, drawing simple conclusions, and working out what an unknown word means using context.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"The school library opens at eight every morning. On Mondays and Wednesdays it is open until five o'clock, on other days it closes at three. During the holidays the library is completely closed."

Which day can you borrow books latest in the afternoon?
questions.opener: The answer is stated directly in the text — look for the day mentioned together with the latest time.
questions.explanation: The text says the library is open until five o'clock on Mondays and Wednesdays — of the options, Wednesday is the only one of these. Tuesday, Thursday and Friday belong to "other days", when it already closes at three.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"Getting too little sleep makes it harder to concentrate at school. Many teenagers sit with their phones late in the evening and therefore fall asleep later than they intended. Researchers recommend putting the screen away an hour before bedtime. That makes it easier to fall asleep."

What is the text mainly about?
questions.opener: Ask yourself what ALL the sentences together are about, not just one of them.
choices: That phones should be banned in schools
That all teenagers fall asleep late
That researchers think teenagers are lazy
That too little sleep affects school, and that evening screen use is one cause
questions.explanation: The text links sleep, concentration and evening phone use, and gives a piece of advice. Banning phones in schools is never mentioned — the text is about evenings, not lesson time.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"Noor glanced towards the door every time it opened. She had laid out the plates an hour ago, and the food still sat untouched on the table. The phone lay silent beside the glass."

What can you understand about Noor?
questions.opener: The text doesn't state it directly — what do the details reveal about what she is doing?
choices: She is waiting for someone who hasn't arrived
She is hungry and is just about to start eating
She is angry at her phone
She is in the middle of cooking
questions.explanation: The glances at the door, the untouched food and the silent phone together show that she is waiting for someone who is late. That she is about to eat doesn't fit — the food has sat out for an hour without her touching it.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"The hike turned out longer than they had thought. When they finally reached the cabin, everyone was exhausted. Elias threw off his backpack and sank down onto the bunk without having the energy to take off his shoes."

What does the word "exhausted" mean in the text?
questions.opener: Read the sentences before and after the word — what are the people doing, and what does that say about how they feel?
questions.explanation: The hike was long and Elias doesn't even have the energy to take off his shoes — the context shows that "exhausted" means very tired. Being hungry isn't mentioned at all in the text, even though it might sound plausible after a long hike.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"The class is going to the nature reserve on Thursday. The bus leaves from the school at nine o'clock, so everyone should be there at quarter to nine. Bring a packed lunch, rain gear and sturdy shoes. Phones may be brought but should stay in the bag during the hike."

What time should the students be at school?
questions.opener: Two times are mentioned — read carefully which one applies to the bus and which applies to the students.
questions.explanation: The text says the bus leaves at nine o'clock and that everyone should therefore be there at quarter to nine. Nine o'clock is thus the bus's departure time, not the meeting time.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"It was the first time Milo was going to play a match with the new team. He retied his shoelaces three times. His hands were cold even though the sun was shining, and he only answered with a nod when the coach asked if he was ready."

How does Milo most likely feel?
questions.opener: Which small details in the body and behaviour usually reveal a feeling?
questions.explanation: Retying his shoes over and over, having cold hands in sunshine, and barely managing to answer all point to nervousness before the first match. He is hardly cold — the text explicitly says the sun was shining.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer in one sentence: "The school's after-school club is open every Tuesday and Thursday after the end of the school day. There you can play games, do crafts, or just hang out. The club is free, but you must sign up with Sofia in the office before coming the first time."

What must you do before going to the after-school club for the first time, and why isn't it enough to just show up?
questions.opener: First find the sentence that contains the word "must" — that's where the requirement is.
questions.answer: You must sign up with Sofia in the office before your first visit, since the text says that signing up is required before you come the first time — so it isn't enough to just turn up.
steps: Read the question first so you know what you're looking for: a requirement before the first visit.
Search the text for signal words like "must", "should" or "before".
The last sentence contains the requirement: signing up with Sofia in the office.
Check that nothing else in the text contradicts the answer — the club is free, but signing up is still required.
Write the answer in your own sentence and back it up with what the text actually says.

questions.prompt: How do you go about answering a reading comprehension question?
questions.opener: Four habits that help you find the right answer more often.
questions.answer: Read the question first — then you know what you're looking for in the text. Finding information: the answer is often stated directly · go back and point to the sentence instead of guessing from memory. Main message: ask what the WHOLE text is about, not just one detail · the point is often in the first or last sentence. Conclusions: build on clues in the text — what the people do, say and feel · never on your own guesses. Unknown words: read the surrounding sentences · test which option fits the context. Warning: answer options that sound plausible but are never mentioned in the text are wrong.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"The swimming pool is open to the public Monday to Friday from 6 am to 8 pm. On weekends the opening hours are 9 am to 3 pm. Every Wednesday from 6 to 7 pm it is reserved for swimming lessons."

When is the pool open to the public on Saturdays?
questions.opener: The answer is stated directly in the text — look for the time that goes with weekends.
choices: The pool is closed on Saturdays
questions.explanation: The text says the weekend opening hours are 9 am to 3 pm. 6 am to 8 pm applies on weekdays, and 6 to 7 pm on Wednesdays is reserved for swimming lessons, not the public.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"Many plants in the garden had wilted in the summer heat. Despite regular watering, not all of them survived. The gardener decided to plant more drought-tolerant plants next year."

What is the text mainly about?
questions.opener: Ask yourself what the whole text is about together, not just the first sentence.
choices: That the gardener never watered the plants
That the summer heat damaged the plants, which made the gardener rethink things for next year
That all the plants in the garden died
That the gardener gave up gardening
questions.explanation: The text links the heat, the watering not being enough, and the decision to choose more drought-tolerant plants going forward. That the gardener stopped watering or gardening isn't true — quite the opposite, they watered regularly and are already planning for next year.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"Ebba read the same page of the book for the third time without remembering what had happened. Outside the window thunder boomed, and she flinched every time lightning lit up the room."

Why does Ebba find it hard to concentrate on the book?
questions.opener: The text doesn't say it directly — what do the details reveal about what's bothering her?
choices: The storm outside is distracting and frightening her
She is tired and wants to sleep
The room is too dark to read in
questions.explanation: Flinching at every flash of lightning and not remembering what she's read, together with the thunder booming outside, show that the storm is what's disrupting her concentration. That the book is bad or the room too dark is never mentioned.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"After the long hike their water bottles were completely empty. Their lips were dry and they longed febrilely for just one sip of water."

What does the word "febrilely" mean in the text?
questions.opener: Read the sentence again — how strong does the longing seem, given the empty bottles and dry lips?
questions.explanation: The empty water bottles and dry lips show that the thirst is strong — the context shows that "febrilely" means very intensely. The word is not about sadness, but about how strong the longing feels.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"The library lends out books for four weeks. Films and games are lent out for one week. If you don't return an item on time, you get a reminder by text message after three days' delay."

How long can you borrow a film for?
questions.opener: Read carefully which loan period applies to books and which applies to films and games.
questions.explanation: The text says films and games are lent out for one week. Four weeks applies to books, and three days is how long a delay is needed before a reminder is sent.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer in one sentence: "Before the competition the team had trained extra hard every day for three weeks. On match day everyone arrived an hour early, wearing their new shirts. The coach smiled broadly as the team walked out onto the field."

What do the details suggest about the team's attitude before the match, and which details support that conclusion?
questions.opener: Look for concrete details in the text that show how the team prepared, not just what they felt.
questions.answer: The details suggest that the team was highly motivated and well prepared for the match, supported by the fact that they trained extra hard for three weeks, arrived early, and the coach smiled broadly.
steps: Read the question first: it's about the team's attitude and which details support the conclusion.
Look for concrete details: extra training for three weeks, arriving an hour early, the coach's smile.
Together these details point toward commitment and good preparation.
Write the answer in one sentence and back it up with at least two of the details.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"Even though she was alone in the house, Nova felt strangely safe. The silence was pleasant, not frightening, and she fell asleep quickly."

What does the word "pleasant" mean in the text?
questions.opener: Read the sentence again — the phrase "not frightening" gives a clue about the opposite meaning.
questions.explanation: The text explicitly says "not frightening" and that Nova felt safe and fell asleep quickly — the context shows that "pleasant" means nice and relaxing.
